How matches are ranked

Best match prioritizes ground imagery, browser-viewable bands, public downloads, then account-required files. Within each access group it prefers timed acquisitions, then proximity to your requested time, lower reported scene cloud and finer nominal pixel spacing. Composite periods and day-only dates are not exact-time captures. Ranking uses loaded records only; a footprint does not guarantee clear or valid pixels at your point.

A LITTLE CONTEXT

See the Earth.
Know what you're seeing.

Start with the whole world: the map opens with a NASA Blue Marble reference mosaic and the archive search has no location restriction. Zoom anywhere and use Search map area, or enter an optional city or coordinate. Worldwide results are a limited catalogue page, not an exhaustive inventory of Earth; narrow the area to find local scenes.

  1. Automatic satellite discovery. Every search checks the connected collections, including Sentinel-1/2/3/5P/6, Landsat, MODIS, ALOS/PALSAR, Resourcesat-1 and CBERS. Some provide downloadable imagery; others provide searchable metadata with account-required downloads. Sentinel-5P measures the atmosphere and Sentinel-6 measures along altimeter tracks; they are not detailed ground photographs. The satellite and data provider are identified on each result.
  2. Availability and suggested matches. Use the timeline to filter loaded results by UTC day. It separates captures from overlapping composites. Best-match cards explain access and time priority, and the sort menu offers closest time, least cloud and finest nominal pixels. Empty days and partial searches do not prove that imagery is absent.
  3. Real band choices. Open a result to see the bands and data layers listed in its metadata. View single bands or available true-colour, vegetation, and SWIR combinations. Band previews use original raster pixels. Supported public INPE bands can be processed through Python for a selected area, even when direct browser access is unavailable. Use Show preview on map to place them in 2D or 3D; large source files and provider failures can still limit processing. Calibration details and display legends are available. Supported surface-reflectance bands can also produce exploratory NDVI, NDWI and NBR previews; these do not apply cloud or shadow masks.
  4. Capture versus composite. Single acquisitions show the provider’s capture time or acquisition interval. Day-only records explicitly say that the exact time is unavailable. MODIS 8-day composites and PALSAR annual mosaics show their coverage period, never an invented capture instant.
  5. Map context. Blue Marble is a reference mosaic, not imagery from your chosen date. Select Daily imagery for the dated Terra/MODIS overview. Scene thumbnails show source tiles; Python band previews show only the selected area. Scene footprints appear on the map. Pin Before A and After B, choose their bands in Imagery, then Display on globe. The swipe slider compares imagery over one reference terrain surface. Use the original files in QGIS for a precise crop or analysis.
  6. Coverage transparency. Each archive reports success, partial results, or unavailability. Empty results from one archive do not hide the others. Connected archives cover many parts of the world; they do not include every satellite or guarantee every location.
WORLDWIDE DATA ACCESS

What this website can search

Search any valid coordinates. The satellite’s country is not a location restriction. A listed mission does not guarantee data over your location or at your requested instant.

Open the guide to load the connected archive list.

Additional provider archives

These are official access routes, not connected search results. Their coverage is not counted as checked by this website.

India · Resourcesat, Cartosat, EOS and other IRS products
ISRO / NRSC Bhoonidhi ↗. Wider Indian holdings require provider access. Its API requires an approved account and authentication. The public Resourcesat-1 holdings searched here are INPE’s regional archive.
China · Gaofen and other national missions
CRESDA ↗. Provider portal; direct integration and download permissions have not been established. CBERS records searched here come from China and Brazil’s joint programme.
Japan · GCOM-C, GCOM-W, ALOS and related products
JAXA G-Portal ↗. Search the provider for additional products and access terms. Earth Window currently searches ALOS/PALSAR annual mosaics, not all Japanese missions.
Landsat · early MSS archive
USGS EarthExplorer ↗ provides Landsat 1–5 MSS Level-1 access. Earth Window’s current Landsat connection is Collection 2 Level 2; early MSS imagery is not included here.
Sentinel · further products and missions
Copernicus Data Space ↗. Only the collections listed above are searched. Sentinel-4/5 and other products are not claimed as connected. Availability depends on the provider’s released catalogue.

Future images do not exist yet. This app does not predict passes, task satellites, track travellers, or show individual people.

Sources: Element 84 Earth Search · NASA GIBS · Microsoft Planetary Computer · USGS Landsat
